DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Displays the NTP global configuration, including administrative enable state, authentication settings, source interface, and VRF. It does not display runtime synchronization state; use "show ntp associations" for that.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command to verify the current NTP global configuration parameters and confirm high-level settings before troubleshooting runtime sync. No arguments are required or accepted.
DOCGEN.EXAMPLE: sonic# show ntp global NTP Configuration: Enabled: True Authentication: False Vrf: default Source Interface: Management0

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Displays all NTP server entries statically configured on the device, including each server's address, NTP protocol version, association type (server or pool), iburst flag, prefer flag, and authentication key ID if assigned. This command shows configured state only; for runtime reachability and stratum information use "show ntp associations".
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command to audit the list of configured NTP servers and verify per-server parameters such as version, iburst, prefer, key, and association type. No arguments are required or accepted.
DOCGEN.EXAMPLE: sonic# show ntp server NTP Servers: Address Version Association Iburst Prefer Key 192.0.2.1 4 server enabled False - 192.0.2.2 4 server disabled False - 2001:db8::1 4 pool enabled True 1

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Displays the runtime NTP peer association table showing synchronization state for each configured server or pool entry. Output includes reference ID, stratum, poll interval, reach register, delay, offset, and jitter for each peer. The currently selected synchronization source is indicated with a '*' prefix. This command reflects live operational state from the NTP daemon and may differ from configured state shown by "show ntp server".
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command to verify NTP is actively synchronizing with a peer and to diagnose synchronization issues. No arguments are required or accepted. Confirm that global NTP is enabled and servers are configured before interpreting output.

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Administratively enables the NTP service on the device. When enabled, the NTP daemon is activated and the device attempts to synchronize its system clock with the configured NTP servers. NTP is disabled by default; this command must be issued before synchronization can occur.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command to turn on the NTP service after completing server and optional authentication configuration. No arguments are required or accepted. To disable NTP, use "no ntp enable".

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Administratively disables the NTP service on the device. The NTP daemon is stopped and the device will no longer synchronize its system clock with NTP servers. All NTP server and authentication configuration is preserved; the service can be re-enabled with "ntp enable" without reconfiguring those parameters.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command to stop NTP synchronization without removing server or authentication configuration. No arguments are required or accepted.

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Enables mandatory NTP authentication. When active, the device only accepts time synchronization from NTP servers that supply a valid, trusted authentication key. Both authentication keys ("ntp authentication-key") and trusted-key designations ("ntp trusted-key") must be configured for authentication to function correctly.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command after defining authentication keys and trusted-key entries to enforce authenticated NTP. No arguments are required or accepted. To disable authentication enforcement, use "no ntp authenticate". Note: disabling authentication does not remove configured keys or trusted-key entries.

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Disables mandatory NTP authentication enforcement. The device will accept time synchronization from servers regardless of whether they supply an authentication key. Previously configured authentication keys and trusted-key entries are preserved and can be re-enabled without reconfiguration by issuing "ntp authenticate".
DOCGEN.USAGE: Use this command to turn off authentication enforcement while retaining key definitions. No arguments are required or accepted.

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Defines an NTP authentication key by associating a numeric key ID with an encryption algorithm and a shared secret password. Keys defined here are referenced by "ntp trusted-key" to mark them as acceptable for synchronization, and by "ntp server ... key" to associate them with a specific server entry. Supported encryption types: md5, sha1, sha256, sha384, sha512.
DOCGEN.USAGE:
Required arguments (all three are mandatory): <key-id> - Integer key identifier in the range 1�65535. <auth-type> - Encryption algorithm: md5, sha1, sha256, sha384, or sha512. <password> - Shared secret string. Pipe characters (|) are not permitted.
A key is not enforced for authentication until it is also designated trusted with "ntp trusted-key <key-id>". To remove a key, use "no ntp authentication-key <key-id>".

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Removes the NTP authentication key associated with the specified key ID. If the key is currently referenced by a trusted-key entry or by a server configuration, those references should be removed first to avoid inconsistent state. Deleting a key does not automatically remove associated trusted-key or server-key references.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Required argument: <key-id> - Integer key identifier in the range 1�65535; must match a previously configured authentication key.

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Designates an authentication key (previously defined with "ntp authentication-key") as trusted. Only trusted keys are accepted for NTP authentication when "ntp authenticate" is enabled. Multiple keys can be trusted simultaneously. A key must exist via "ntp authentication-key" before it can be made trusted.
DOCGEN.USAGE:
Required argument: <key-id> - Integer key identifier in the range 1�65535; must correspond to an existing authentication key entry.
To revoke trust from a key without removing its definition, use "no ntp trusted-key <key-id>".

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Removes the trusted designation from the specified authentication key. The key definition itself (type and password) is retained under "ntp authentication-key" and can be re-trusted without reconfiguration. Once untrusted, the key will no longer be accepted for NTP authentication even if still referenced by a server configuration.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Required argument: <key-id> - Integer key identifier in the range 1�65535; must correspond to an existing trusted-key entry.

COMMAND.name: ntp server

PARAM.name: server-addr
PARAM.help: NTP server IP address or hostname

COMMAND.ACTION: python3 $SONIC_CLI_ROOT/sonic-cli-ntp.py set_ntp_server ${server-addr} version:${version-value} association-type:${assoc-value} iburst:${iburst} key:${key-value} prefer:${prefer}

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Adds an NTP time source to the device configuration. The time source can be specified as an IPv4 address, IPv6 address, or a fully-qualified domain name (FQDN). Optional parameters control the NTP protocol version, association type (unicast server or pool), initial burst behavior, authentication key, and server preference. Multiple servers can be configured simultaneously.
DOCGEN.USAGE:
Required argument: <server-addr> - NTP server IPv4/IPv6 address or hostname/FQDN.
Optional arguments (all optional, combinable in any order): version <3|4> - NTP protocol version for this server (default: 4). association <server|pool> - Association mode: unicast server or pool (default: server). iburst - Send a burst of packets at startup for faster initial sync. key <key-id> - Authentication key ID (1�65535); the key must be defined with "ntp authentication-key" and trusted with "ntp trusted-key". prefer - Mark this server as the preferred synchronization source.
To remove a server entry, use "no ntp server <server-addr>".
DOCGEN.EXAMPLE: sonic(config)# ntp server 192.0.2.1 version 4 iburst prefer key 1

PARAM.name: server-addr
PARAM.help: NTP server IP address or hostname

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Removes a previously configured NTP server entry identified by its IP address or hostname. All per-server parameters (version, association type, iburst, key, prefer) associated with that entry are also removed. Other server entries and global NTP configuration are not affected.
DOCGEN.USAGE: Required argument: <server-addr> - The IP address or hostname of the NTP server to remove. Must exactly match the value used when the server was added.

COMMAND.name: ntp source-interface
COMMAND.help: Configure NTP source interface to pick the source IP used for NTP packets

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Specifies the interface whose primary IP address is used as the source address for outgoing NTP packets. This setting applies globally to all NTP server associations. If no source interface is configured, the device selects the source address based on the routing table (outgoing interface toward each server). Common values are management interfaces (e.g., Management0) or loopback interfaces.
DOCGEN.USAGE:
Required argument: <interface-type> <interface-id> - Interface type and identifier Supported types: Ethernet, Loopback, Management, PortChannel The interface must exist and have an IP address assigned.
To remove the source interface configuration, use "no ntp source-interface".
DOCGEN.EXAMPLE: sonic(config)# ntp source-interface Management 0 sonic(config)# ntp source-interface Loopback 0 sonic(config)# ntp source-interface Ethernet 0

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Removes the configured NTP source interface. After removal, the device reverts to default source address selection, choosing the source IP based on the best route toward each NTP server. NTP server entries and other global configuration are not affected.
DOCGEN.USAGE: No arguments are required or accepted. Use this command to revert NTP source selection to default routing-table-based behavior.

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Binds NTP operation to the specified VRF, causing all NTP control traffic to be sent and received within that VRF's routing domain. Supported values are "mgmt" (management VRF) and "default" (the default routing instance). Binding NTP to the management VRF is typical for out-of-band management environments. Only one VRF can be active for NTP at a time.
DOCGEN.USAGE:
Required argument: <vrf-name> - Name of the VRF to use for NTP: "mgmt" or "default". The specified VRF must exist before applying this configuration.
To remove the VRF binding and revert to default VRF behavior, use "no ntp vrf".

DOCGEN.DESCRIPTION: Removes the NTP VRF binding, reverting NTP to operate within the default VRF routing domain. NTP server entries, authentication configuration, and other global settings are not affected. After removal, NTP traffic will be routed through the default routing table.
DOCGEN.USAGE: No arguments are required or accepted. Use this command to remove an existing VRF association and restore default VRF behavior for NTP.
